meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste the time. Why was a zero entered on Owen's essay before anyone called me?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.

I'm writing down September 24. A timed class piece against a take-home essay: those are two different conditions, and I'll want both documents in front of me. You still haven't told me why the zero went in before you called me.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
I'm writing down that the checker is off the table. A version history is a document, so what does it show? I want the dates and times.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed in the meeting that the detector result is off the table and that you are relying on the writing and the version history. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn, that I receive an apology, and that I be given both writing samples and the version history with dates and times. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, agreeing to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the documents in her hands.
What moved her: dropping the detector and naming the September 24 sample with its word count gave a small bit of ground, because it was specific and dated, but she had seen none of it on paper yet.
What cost ground: never answering why the zero went in before she was called, even after she asked, which left her main grievance standing.
Try next time: in your first turn, own the zero going in before the call in one sentence, then put the version history in front of her with its times.
